sources.note: SILENT. Chapter Two 'Phonology' (pp. 8-21) has 14 sections (consonantal phonemes, vocalic phonemes, distributional restrictions, stop-lenition, morphophoneme W, stop-insertion, hardening of /y/, cluster rules, vowel-shifting, y-deletion, vowel-cluster contraction, semivowel-insertion, reduplication, nasal-deletion) and no stress/accent/prosody section; whole-text a full-text search for stress/accent (incl. spaced-scanned variants) finds no phonological use of 'stress' or 'accent'. Nearest remarks: p. 11 'Mara tends to phonetically lengthen vowels in open initial syllables in bisyllabic words.…

sources.citation: WALS Online (Dryer & Haspelmath 2013), language wrn 'Warndarang' (= wand1263); StressTyp2 v1 SQL dump (Goedemans, Heinz & van der Hulst 2015).
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: No stress data: WALS has no 14A-17A values for wrn; StressTyp2 has 'wnd' only in its ISO code table, no language record.

Phonology section covers clusters, initial phonemes, stops, reduplication; nothing on stress or prosody. Reference list adds Capell 1960 (Oceania 30: 206-224, texts), Heath 1976, Sharpe 1972, Sharpe 1976.

sources.note: SILENT on Warndarang stress. Ch. 2 sections 4-7 and 11 treat Nunggubuyu/Warndarang phonology (stops, glottal stops, vowels, other rules). The only phonological 'stress' mention (p. 62) is that Nunggubuyu vowel length 'is manifested by minor stress, intonation, and length variations'; the same passage says Warndarang 'allows long vowels at no level'.

sources.citation: Glottolog 5.x languoid page wand1263 and reference page 104191 (Capell 1941-43).
sources.note: Bibliographic only: Glottolog's descriptive refs are Heath 1980 (grammar, twice), Heath 1987 and Harvey 1997 (noun-class papers); Capell 1941-43 Oceania 12: 364-392, 13: 24-51 covers Wandarang among 24+ Arnhem Land languages. No stress content seen.
